en.title: Rockstar's GTA 6 Union Battle: Mole Spied on Workers for 2.5 Years
en.summary: Rockstar Games is embroiled in a legal battle following the dismissal of 34 employees. The company revealed it had a mole embedded in a worker-organized Discord server for over two and a half years.
en.body:
The development of **Grand Theft Auto 6**, slated for a 2026 release, has been overshadowed by a significant legal dispute between **Rockstar Games** and former employees. In October 2025, the studio terminated 34 staff members, predominantly based in the UK, citing "gross misconduct" and alleging they jeopardized confidential information through activity on a Discord server established by union organizers.

Now, as the case proceeds through an employment tribunal in Glasgow, **Take-Two Interactive**, Rockstar's parent company, has disclosed a startling detail: the company maintained a mole, or "whistleblower," within the union's private server for an extended period of "over two and a half years." This revelation comes as part of extensive legal filings, totaling over 100 pages of claims and counterclaims, which aim to contextualize the dismissals and the alleged union-busting motives behind them. The ousted employees and their representatives contend that their terminations were designed to prevent the union from achieving official recognition under UK law.

## The Discord Infiltration

The employment tribunal is set to delve into thousands of pages of evidence, offering a rare glimpse into the internal machinations at **Rockstar Games**. The presence of an informant within the workers' private communication channel raises serious questions about the company's approach to labor organizing. While **Rockstar** maintains its actions were justified due to risks of leaks, the union argues this was a deliberate tactic to undermine their efforts to gain collective bargaining power. The prolonged duration of the mole's operation suggests a sophisticated and patient strategy by the company.

## Fan Reaction and Industry Implications

News of the mole has sent ripples through the gaming community, particularly among the passionate fanbase eagerly awaiting **GTA 6**. Many fans express concern over the ethical implications of such surveillance, questioning the environment fostered within one of the industry's most prominent studios. This case could set a precedent for how game development companies handle unionization efforts and employee privacy. The extended development cycle for **GTA 6** has already been a topic of discussion, with some reports suggesting a potential delay to November 19th, 2026, though this remains unconfirmed by **Rockstar**.

## What's Next

The employment tribunal in Glasgow will continue to hear evidence in the coming weeks. The outcome of this legal battle could have significant repercussions for employee rights and unionization within the video game industry, potentially influencing future labor relations at **Rockstar Games** and beyond.

content_raw: Back in October 2025, GTA 6 developers Rockstar fired a group of 34, mostly UK-based employees on a charge of "gross misconduct", alleging that they had risked the leaking of confidential information while posting on a Discord server set up by union organisers. The ousted UK workers and their representatives have since taken Rockstar to court, accusing the company of getting rid of them to stop their union gaining enough members to win official recognition under UK law. This week, both parties filed opening submissions at an employment tribunal in Glasgow , which Rockstar parent company Take-Two Interactive have emailed to RPS and Game Developer , among others. Taken together, the filings amount to over 100 pages of claims and counterclaims, with thousands of pages of evidence to be discussed in the coming weeks. Amongst other things, the docs give us more sense of events leading up to the dismissals, including the revelation that Rockstar had a mole or "whistleblower" passing them information on the people using the Discord server.
